children: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT, Financials), the software and cloud powerhouse behind Azure and Office, is handing stockholders a smidge more cash. The business upped its quarterly dividend 7.7% to 98 cents a share from 91 cents.
That may not seem like a shift. Microsoft's forecast dividend yield is just shy of 0.79%. But the timing is what makes it more interesting.

Microsoft is spending substantially on the data centers and computing power required for its AI business. These are big-ticket projects, and investors have been watching closely to see how that spending affects the company's cash priorities.
For the moment it seems Microsoft is happy to do both. It can keep plowing big money into AI infrastructure while raising what it gives back to shareholders.
The new dividend will be paid Dec. 10 to stockholders of record Nov. 19. Microsoft is not the most generous dividend payer for income investors. And actually that's not the draw here.
The dividend hike is another reminder of the amount of cash the corporation continues to earn, even in one of the greatest investment cycles in its history.
Now investors will be looking to see if that balance can be maintained as Microsoft increases investment on AI.

title: Microsoft raises its dividend 8% as cash returns keep climbing
